definitions.explanation: The process of absorbing into or becoming similar to a surrounding culture, group, or environment. Also used in biology for the metabolic process of converting nutrients into body tissue.

examples.japanese: {移民|いみん}が{現地|げんち}の{文化|ぶんか}に{同化|どうか}する。
examples.english: Immigrants assimilate into the local culture.

examples.japanese: {同化|どうか}{政策|せいさく}は{少数民族|しょうすうみんぞく}の{文化|ぶんか}を{消|け}してしまう{危険|きけん}がある。
examples.english: Assimilation policies risk erasing the culture of ethnic minorities.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}で{長|なが}く{暮|く}らすうちに、いつの{間|ま}にか{現地|げんち}の{生活|せいかつ}に{同化|どうか}していた。
examples.english: After living abroad for a long time, I had unknowingly assimilated into the local way of life.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a suru verb: {同化|どうか}する (to assimilate). Most commonly appears in discussions of cultural integration, immigration, and social policy. In biology, it refers to anabolism — the process by which organisms convert nutrients into body tissue.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同化|どうか}する: to assimilate
- {同化|どうか}{政策|せいさく}: assimilation policy
- {文化的|ぶんかてき}{同化|どうか}: cultural assimilation
- ～に{同化|どうか}する: to assimilate into ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
{同化|どうか} implies becoming the same as the surrounding group. {適応|てきおう} (adaptation) means adjusting to an environment without necessarily losing one's own identity. {融合|ゆうごう} (fusion) implies mutual blending of both sides.
